children: Electricity storage and software provider Fluence
will be reporting results this Monday after market hours. Here’s what you need to know.

Fluence Energy missed analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $649.8 million, up 7.9% year on year. It was an underwhelming quarter for the company, with full-year revenue guidance missing analysts’ expectations significantly and full-year EBITDA guidance missing analysts’ expectations significantly.
Is Fluence Energy a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Fluence Energy’s revenue to decline 18.2% year on year, a further deceleration from the 15.2% decrease it recorded in the same quarter last year.
Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings.

Looking at Fluence Energy’s peers in the renewable energy segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Sunrun delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 51.7%, beating analysts’ expectations by 46.5%, and Bloom Energy reported revenues up 138%, topping estimates by 14.6%. Sunrun traded up 12.3% following the results while Bloom Energy was down 11.2%.

In the last year or so, investors have shifted their focus from one macro dynamic to the next (AI disintermediation and AI investment to geopolitical conflict, interest rates, and the health of the wider economy). While some of the renewable energy stocks have shown solid performance in this choppy environment, the group has generally underperformed, with share prices down 6.1% on average over the last month. Fluence Energy is down 36% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $7.95 (compared to the current share price of $3.58).
